summary: A group-versus-group question game with five male guests, and the most repeated complaint is that it ended too soon — several say they were settling in and it was over, and one adds that the food element could be dropped entirely because the conversation was enough. The warmest cluster is about the group protecting Dream: when a brutal question landed on her, nobody pressed, and both hosts and guests helped her out, which viewers call out as the nicest moment. One guest is singled out as the troublemaker who drives the comedy. Cross-series funnelling appears again, with viewers asking for two of the guests to be moved onto the car show. Behind-the-scenes footage included in the edit is specifically appreciated.

audience_signals: Viewers say the gimmick is unnecessary — the conversation alone would hold them, which means the food-punishment device is cost without benefit
Kindness on camera reads as strongly as comedy: the moment the group shielded a host from a question is the second most-liked theme in the thread
Multi-guest ensembles create their own cross-booking demand, with viewers picking out individuals to move to other formats
Runtime is again the complaint — this audience consistently wants more minutes, not fewer
